source.author: hor
source.text: Iustum et tenacem propositi virum non civium ardor prava iubentium, non voltus instantis tyranni mente quatit solida neque Auster, dux inquieti turbidus Hadriae, nec fulminantis magna manus Iovis:
source.text_original: Iustum et tenacem propositi virum / non civium ardor prava iubentium, / non voltus instantis tyranni / mente quatit solida neque Auster, / dux inquieti turbidus Hadriae, / nec fulminantis magna manus Iovis: /
source.text_english: The just man, steadfast in purpose, is not shaken in his firm mind by the citizens’ zeal commanding what is wrong, nor by the face of a threatening tyrant, nor by Auster, the stormy leader of restless Hadria, nor by the mighty hand of thundering Iovis.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: nisi forte delirare illis uidetur Flaccus in lyricis, cum dicit: iustum et tenacem propositi uirum non ciuium ardor praua iubentium, uon uultus instantis tyranni mente quatit solida.
reuse.text_original: nisi forte delirare illis uidetur Flaccus in lyricis, cum dicit: iustum et tenacem propositi uirum non ciuium ardor praua iubentium, uon uultus instantis tyranni mente quatit solida.
reuse.text_english: unless perhaps Flaccus seems to them to be raving in the lyrics when he says: neither the zeal of citizens giving wrong commands, nor the face of the threatening tyrant, shakes from his firm mind the man who is just and steadfast in his purpose.
